title: Higher Ground
alsoKnownAs: I’m Pressing on the Upward Way
description: Higher Ground in Tonic Solfa to HIGHER GROUND: the solfa with the words, staff notation, the four verses and the refrain, and a piano.
about: Johnson Oatman Jr. wrote the words, first published in 1898. The tune, HIGHER GROUND, is by Charles Hutchinson Gabriel (1902).
underlay: I’m press-ing on the up-ward way, New heights I’m gain-ing ev-ery day; Still pray-ing as I’m on-ward bound, “Lord, plant my feet on high-er ground.” Lord, lift me up and let me stand, By faith, on Heav-en’s ta-ble-land, A high-er plane than I have found; Lord, plant my feet on high-er ground.

lines: I’m pressing on the upward way,
New heights I’m gaining every day;
Still praying as I’m onward bound,
“Lord, plant my feet on higher ground.”

verses.label: Refrain
lines: Lord, lift me up and let me stand,
By faith, on Heaven’s tableland,
A higher plane than I have found;
Lord, plant my feet on higher ground.
My heart has no desire to stay
Where doubts arise and fears dismay;
Though some may dwell where those abound,
My prayer, my aim, is higher ground.
I want to live above the world,
Though Satan’s darts at me are hurled;
For faith has caught the joyful sound,
The song of saints on higher ground.
I want to scale the utmost height
And catch a gleam of glory bright;
But still I’ll pray till heav’n I’ve found,
“Lord, plant my feet on higher ground.”
